intro_html: A good beef ragu is the kind of meal that tastes expensive and cooks for almost nothing. Lean ground beef simmers with carrots, onion, and crushed tomatoes into a rich sauce, then tosses with penne and a little parmesan. It runs around $5.07 a serving (at everyday cost) with 55 grams of protein and makes 14 bowls.
cost_closing_html: About $5.07 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Each of the 14 servings gives you 55 grams of protein at 603 calories.
upsell_html: Slow-simmered flavor, weeknight ease, and a price that lets you cook it as often as you like. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: Store-brand canned tomatoes make a sauce every bit as good as the name brands. Buy the cheapest crushed tomatoes and tomato paste and save the money.
A wedge of parmesan grated at home costs less and tastes better than the pre-grated stuff. Buy a block of parmesan and grate it yourself.
Dried pasta is one of the cheapest foods in the store. Stock up on boxed pasta whenever it goes on sale.
make_it: Brown the ground beef in a large skillet, breaking it up, then drain the grease.
Add the chopped onion, carrots, and garlic and cook until softened.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, beef broth, and Italian seasoning.
Simmer for 25 to 30 minutes until the sauce is thick and rich.
Cook the penne until just tender, then toss it with the sauce.
Finish with a shower of parmesan over the top.
